main_text.l: 1. Hamza (ء) est servus Elif mobilis, cui
cum vocali appositum, motum ejus actualem
significat, ut أن، أن، أن an, on, in, & sine
sil. quod | sit radicale, & naturâ suâ mobile,
ut [?]لمين jamen. Sæpè tamen omittitur ut
superfluum, quia motus | ex vocali adjecta
facilè percipitur, sicut & posita Hamza, illud |
sæpè omittitur, ita ut pro eodem usurpa-
tur, & in pronuntiatione idem valet : idque
1, In sine, cum Hamza habet ante se unam
ex literis [illegible, ~3 letters] ut [?]مـاون maon, pro [?]سـاون,
2, In medio post literam vocali carentem,
duplex occurrit | quarum prius movetur, in

page.notes: The Arabic and Hebrew-style forms are copied as best the scan allows; the vowel points and several letters in the Arabic words are doubtful and marked [?]. The Latin text is clear. Long s has been written as plain s throughout.
